EA201.question: What is the advantage of the binary number system over the decimal number system in electronic circuits?
EA201.answer_a: The binary digits 0 and 1 can be represented as two electrical states and can therefore be processed easily by switching elements (e.g. transistors).
EA201.answer_b: The accuracy of the binary system (with two digits) is higher by a factor of 5 than that of the decimal system (with 10 digits).
EA201.answer_c: The intermediate range between 0 and 1 can be represented with high accuracy by analogue amplifier circuits.
EA201.answer_d: More than one bit of information can be transmitted per digit (1 binary digit allows 8 decimal digits to be transmitted).

AB109.question: How does the depletion region behave in the semiconductor diode shown here?

AB108.question: The following picture shows the basic structure of a semiconductor diode. How is the depletion layer formed?
AB108.answer_a: At the junction, electrons migrate from the N-type side into the P-type side. This partly reduces the excess of electrons on the N-type side and partly neutralises the deficiency of electrons on the P-type side. An insulating layer forms on both sides of the boundary.
AB108.answer_b: At the junction, electrons migrate from the P-type side into the N-type side. This partly reduces the excess of electrons on the P-type side and partly neutralises the deficiency of electrons on the N-type side. An insulating layer forms on both sides of the boundary.
AB108.answer_c: At the junction, atoms migrate from the P-type side into the N-type side. This reduces the deficiency of atoms on the P-type side and increases the deficiency of atoms on the N-type side. A conducting layer forms on both sides of the boundary.
AB108.answer_d: At the junction, atoms migrate from the N-type side into the P-type side. This reduces the deficiency of atoms on the N-type side and increases the deficiency of atoms on the P-type side. A conducting layer forms on both sides of the boundary.

AB105.question: What is meant by doping?
AB105.answer_a: Introducing foreign atoms of a different chemical valency into a base semiconductor material in order to provide free charge carriers.
AB105.answer_b: Removing atoms from the base semiconductor material in order to reduce its electrical conductivity.
AB105.answer_c: Introducing magnetic north or south poles into a base semiconductor material in order to increase its inductance.
AB105.answer_d: Removing impurities from a base semiconductor material in order to generate electrons.

AB104.question: What are semiconductor materials?
AB104.answer_a: Some substances (e.g. silicon) are good insulators in the pure state at room temperature. However, small additions of suitable other substances (e.g. boron, phosphorus) or high temperatures turn them into conductors.
AB104.answer_b: Some substances (e.g. silicon) are good conductors in the pure state at room temperature. However, small additions of suitable other substances (e.g. boron, phosphorus) or high temperatures reduce their conductivity.
AB104.answer_c: Some substances (e.g. silicon) are good conductors in the pure state at room temperature. Small additions of suitable other substances (e.g. bismuth, tellurium) halve their resistance.
AB104.answer_d: Some substances (e.g. silicon) are good electrolytes in the pure state at room temperature. With small additions of suitable other substances (e.g. bismuth, tellurium) they can be made into either N-type or P-type material for the anodes or cathodes of batteries.

AB103.question: How does the resistance of a metal normally change with temperature?
AB103.answer_a: The resistance rises as the temperature increases, i.e. the temperature coefficient is positive.

AB103.answer_c: The resistance does not change as the temperature increases, i.e. the temperature coefficient is zero.
AB103.answer_d: The resistance oscillates as the temperature increases, i.e. the temperature coefficient is complex.

NB304.question: Which polarisations are usually distinguished in the propagation of radio waves in amateur radio, and why should they be taken into account?
